name: Light Chain Deposition Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Light Chain Deposition Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Detection of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine by immunofixation electrophoresis
Histological demonstration of non-amyloid monoclonal light chain deposits in affected tissues by immunofluorescence or immunohistochemistry
Evidence of organ dysfunction attributable to light chain deposition (e.g., renal impairment, cardiac involvement)
Exclusion of systemic amyloidosis by Congo red staining and electron microscopy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine, histological confirmation of light chain deposits in tissue, and clinical evidence of organ dysfunction related to deposits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires differentiation from AL amyloidosis and other monoclonal gammopathies.

laboratory: Monoclonal light chains detected by serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or enlarged kidneys
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; associated with plasma cell dyscrasia
other: Renal biopsy with immunofluorescence showing linear monoclonal light chain deposits along basement membranes
Negative Congo red staining excluding amyloidosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of Congo red positive amyloid deposits
Different ultrastructural fibril morphology on electron microscopy
Involvement of heavy chains or combined heavy and light chains
May have more extensive systemic involvement

redFlags: Evidence of systemic organ dysfunction due to light chain deposits
